subject: Review: international data illustrations for Hosted API privacy copy
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Corp Legal <legal@acme.com>
Date: Sat, 05 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Review: international data illustrations for Hosted API privacy copy

Hi team,

Quick ask: legal asked for a shorter set of public-facing examples that explain how customer data flows when they use the Hosted API + Console (for sales collateral and the privacy page). The current draft is technical and mentions DPA/SCCs in passing — they want plain-language vignettes that non-legal readers (developers and product managers) can scan quickly.

Goals:
- 3 short examples (<= 2 sentences each) showing common flows: API request to model in-host, API with customer-managed keys, and admin console log access for billing/debugging.
- One short line explaining cross-border transfers and the mechanisms (SCCs, adequacy, UK addendum) without legalese.
- A console tooltip snippet (40–80 chars) that clarifies where residency/transfer info lives.

I attached a first pass (draft_privacy_snippets_v1.md) and a 1-page SCCs explainer (sccs-summary.pdf).

Please review and add edits inline in Drive link or reply here. Tagging Acme Legal for any redlines that would affect customers in EU/UK.

Thanks,
Kim

Attachments: draft_privacy_snippets_v1.md (markdown), sccs-summary.pdf (pdf)

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Acme Corp Legal <legal@acme.com>
Date: Sat, 05 Dec 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Review: international data illustrations for Hosted API privacy copy

Thanks Kim — good initiative. I made inline edits to the draft and proposed three short vignettes below (keeping them conversational). A couple of legal questions are inline as well.

Proposed short examples (editable):
1) "When you send text to our Hosted API, tokens are processed by the selected model in the region you choose; temporary inference logs may be retained briefly for quality and abuse detection unless you opt into longer retention."
2) "If you enable customer-managed keys, the model service processes tokens but encryption keys for stored data are controlled by your cloud KMS."
3) "Console admins can see metadata (timestamps, request IDs, billing usage) to debug and invoice, but payloads are not displayed unless you explicitly export them."

Cross-border line (suggestion):
"We may transfer data between countries to serve requests; where required, we rely on standard transfer safeguards (e.g., SCCs or recognized adequacy decisions) — details in the DPA."

Questions/notes:
- Acme asked about explicit mention of the UK Addendum and whether we should call out the EU Commission SCCs by name.
- Vivek/Stephanie: console tooltip candidates attached (console-ui-snippets.png) — can we fit the residency pointer there?

I'll hold on further edits until legal confirms the transfer phrasing.

Laura

Date: Mon, 07 Dec 2026 08:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Review: international data illustrations for Hosted API privacy copy

Hi Kimberly and team,

Thanks for sharing. The plain-language vignettes are helpful. A few items from Acme's side:

- We appreciate the SCCs reference. For our procurement/legal team, an explicit mention that Redwood supports the EU Commission SCCs (and the UK Addendum where applicable) would be useful.
- Can you add one sentence saying whether customer-supplied content may be transferred to subprocessors (i.e., does Redwood allow subprocessors to process content outside the EU/UK)? A short affirmative + pointer to the subprocessor list is sufficient.
- Also: would you confirm if inference logs used for abuse detection are ever stored outside of the selected region? That is a gating question for our security review.

If you prefer, we can provide the precise language we prefer for the procurement packet.

Best,
Marina Alvarez
Acme Corp — Legal Ops

On Sat, 05 Dec 2026 at 09:12 AM Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com> wrote:

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Corp Legal <legal@acme.com>, DataTransit Ltd <compliance@datatransit.io>
Date: Mon, 07 Dec 2026 11:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Review: international data illustrations for Hosted API privacy copy

Thanks — great feedback. Quick product notes to align on implementation constraints: 

- Console tooltip: we can include a short residency pointer (50 chars max) that links to the privacy page. The attached console-ui-snippets.png shows placement and two character-length options.
- Subprocessors: we maintain a published subprocessors page; we can add a one-line public callout ("See our subprocessor list for details on where subprocessors process data") and link to it.
- Inference logs: by default, short-lived inference logs used for quality and abuse detection are retained in the same region as the model instance, except when a customer opts into cross-region replication or when troubleshooting requires log transfer for root cause analysis (we record that in audit logs and alert customers).

For the SCCs/UK addendum line, legal: if you confirm the exact phrasing we should use, product can ship the tooltip and the short vignettes by EOD Friday.

Vivek

Attachments: console-ui-snippets.png
Related links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C_example_shared_privacy

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Corp Legal <legal@acme.com>, DataTransit Ltd <compliance@datatransit.io>
Date: Mon, 07 Dec 2026 14:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Review: international data illustrations for Hosted API privacy copy

Nice progress — thanks everyone. Summary and next steps: 

1) Language: Laura's 3 vignettes are approved as the public-facing examples with one small tweak on the second vignette (add explicit phrase: "encryption keys are controlled by your KMS").
2) Transfers: Legal to confirm a single-sentence line we can use: suggested draft from Acme — "We rely on standard transfer safeguards (EU Commission SCCs and applicable UK transfer addenda); see the DPA for details." If legal approves, we'll use that.
3) Subprocessors: Product will add a one-line pointer to the public subprocessor list and include the link in the privacy page.
4) Inference logs: Product confirms region-first retention by default; any cross-region exception will be audited and surfaced to customers. We will add the short sentence Laura proposed on payload export.

Action owners:
- Laura: incorporate the KMS wording and final copy into draft_privacy_snippets_v2.md (due Thu EOD).
- Legal (Acme and DataTransit): please confirm the SCCs + UK addendum line or propose alternative wording (response requested by Thu COB).
- Vivek/Stephanie: finalize console tooltip (50 chars) and link, ship to staging (target Fri).

I will update the HubSpot ticket and attach v2 when ready.

Kim

Attachments: (new) draft_privacy_snippets_v2.md to be added to Drive
